title: Defense dared to answer 3 questions proving VP innocence
summary: As the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte draws to a close, one of the House prosecutors gave an unsolicited advice to their counterparts to help them prove Vice President Sara…

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte on July 30, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — As the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte draws to a close, one of the House prosecutors gave an unsolicited advice to their counterparts to help them prove Vice President Sara Duterte’s innocence against charges of unexplained wealth.

According to Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno, answering three simple questions might help ease the job of the defense in refuting voluminous documents and paper trails about the VP’s questionable assets.

“First, did the Vice President not declare certain assets in her SALN (statement of assets, liabilities and net worth)? Did the VP participate in business while she was VP? And last, did the VP amass wealth that is manifestly disproportionate to her lawful income?” he asked in succession.
Diokno said these are the questions that really matter, because answers to them will determine whether Duterte violated the Constitution or not.
“I think the best way to do it is to stick to what the issues are and to compare those issues with the evidence that’s being presented,” Diokno told “Headstart” on ABS-CBN News yesterday.

“Those are the main questions that must be addressed by the defense and then decided by the court. We are really after the truth and accountability in this proceeding, and we are determined to make sure that that will happen in the days to come,” he emphasized.

The first question concerns whether Duterte accurately disclosed her assets and financial interests in her SALNs, which prosecutors allege contain discrepancies when compared with her financial records.

The second involves Article 7, Section 13 of the Charter, which prohibits her from directly or indirectly participating in business. Prosecutors are examining her business participation and financial interests involving companies linked to her and her husband Manases Carpio.
The third query concerns the prosecution’s forensic accounting findings identifying P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth and undeclared assets involving the Duterte couple from 2022 to 2025.

Article II remains the sole Article of Impeachment being pursued before the Senate impeachment court after the House prosecution panel withdrew the other three articles for them to be able to focus more on the financial allegations.
At the same time, Diokno observed that the defense’s withdrawal of their list of witnesses, particularly bank officials, only left crucial financial records against the VP unchallenged.

“So, their decision not to present means that they have not controverted the evidence that comes from the bank accounts and the other evidence upon which Article II is based,” he said. – With Bella Cariaso, Emmanuel Tupas
